A bill for an act relating to education finance; providing for a grant for economic and financial literacy education and teacher professional development activities; appropriating money.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF MINNESOTA:

Section 1.

[+MINNESOTA COUNCIL ON ECONOMIC EDUCATION; PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT ACTIVITIES. +]

[+Subdivision 1.+]

[+Purpose.+]

[+The Minnesota Council on Economic Education may provide professional development activities to Minnesota's teachers. +]

[+Subd. 2.+]

[+Grant uses.+]

[+Grant money received by the Minnesota Council on Economic Education must be used to: +]

[+(1) provide professional development to and curate and develop curricular resources for: +]

[+(i) Minnesota's kindergarten through grade 12 teachers implementing state graduation standards in learning areas related to economic and financial education; and +]

[+(ii) Minnesota's grade 9 through 12 teachers providing personal finance and consumer protection instruction to students; +]

[+(2) support the direct-to-student ancillary economic and personal finance programs that Minnesota teachers supervise and coach or that the Minnesota Council on Economic Education delivers directly to students; +]

[+(3) support research on the effectiveness of economic and financial literacy education in kindergarten through grade 12 to ensure that the intent of the economics graduation standards and the high school personal finance course requirement is being met, and to identify avenues for improving economic and financial literacy education; and +]

[+(4) support geographically diverse affiliated higher education faculty and higher education-based centers for economic and financial literacy education, including those based at Minnesota State University, Mankato; St. Cloud State University; and St. Catherine University, for activities related to clauses (1) to (3). +]

[+Subd. 3.+]

[+Reporting.+]

[+(a) By February 15 of each year following the receipt of grant money, the Minnesota Council on Economic Education must provide a midyear report to the commissioner of education. By August 15 of each year following receipt of grant money, the Minnesota Council on Economic Education must prepare a year-end report containing at least the information required in paragraph (b) to the commissioner of education in the form and manner prescribed by the commissioner. The commissioner may request additional information as necessary. +]

[+(b) The report must include: +]

[+(1) the number and type of in-person and online teacher professional development opportunities provided by the Minnesota Council on Economic Education or its affiliated state centers; +]

[+(2) a description of the content, length, and location of the programs; +]

[+(3) the number of preservice and licensed teachers receiving professional development through each of these opportunities; +]

[+(4) summaries of evaluations of teacher professional opportunities; +]

[+(5) a list of the number, types, and summary evaluations of the direct-to-student ancillary personal finance programs that are supported by grant money; and +]

[+(6) a description and the status of all economic and financial literacy education research and results of the research supported by grant money. +]

[+(c) The reports required under this subdivision must be prepared and filed according to section 3.195. +]

[+Subd. 4.+]

[+Grant payment schedule.+]

[+The Department of Education must pay one-half of the amount of any grant money awarded to the Minnesota Council on Economic Education by August 15 of each fiscal year for which the money is appropriated and the other half must be paid by February 15 of that same fiscal year. The Minnesota Council on Economic Education must submit its fiscal reporting in the form and manner specified by the commissioner. The commissioner may request additional financial information as necessary. +]

Sec. 2. [+APPROPRIATIONS; MINNESOTA COUNCIL ON ECONOMIC EDUCATION. +]

[+Subdivision 1.+]

[+Department of Education.+]

[+The sums indicated in this section are appropriated from the general fund to the Department of Education in the fiscal years designated. +]

[+Subd. 2.+]

[+Minnesota Council on Economic Education.+]

[+For a grant to the Minnesota Council on Economic Education for providing personal finance programs, economic education, and professional development to teachers: +]

bill_text.plain_text:
A bill for an act relating to education finance; providing for a grant for economic and financial literacy education and teacher professional development activities; appropriating money.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF MINNESOTA:

Section 1.

MINNESOTA COUNCIL ON ECONOMIC EDUCATION; PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT ACTIVITIES.

Subdivision 1.

Purpose.

The Minnesota Council on Economic Education may provide professional development activities to Minnesota's teachers.

Subd. 2.

Grant uses.

Grant money received by the Minnesota Council on Economic Education must be used to:

(1) provide professional development to and curate and develop curricular resources for:

(i) Minnesota's kindergarten through grade 12 teachers implementing state graduation standards in learning areas related to economic and financial education; and

(ii) Minnesota's grade 9 through 12 teachers providing personal finance and consumer protection instruction to students;

(2) support the direct-to-student ancillary economic and personal finance programs that Minnesota teachers supervise and coach or that the Minnesota Council on Economic Education delivers directly to students;

(3) support research on the effectiveness of economic and financial literacy education in kindergarten through grade 12 to ensure that the intent of the economics graduation standards and the high school personal finance course requirement is being met, and to identify avenues for improving economic and financial literacy education; and

(4) support geographically diverse affiliated higher education faculty and higher education-based centers for economic and financial literacy education, including those based at Minnesota State University, Mankato; St. Cloud State University; and St. Catherine University, for activities related to clauses (1) to (3).

Subd. 3.

Reporting.

(a) By February 15 of each year following the receipt of grant money, the Minnesota Council on Economic Education must provide a midyear report to the commissioner of education. By August 15 of each year following receipt of grant money, the Minnesota Council on Economic Education must prepare a year-end report containing at least the information required in paragraph (b) to the commissioner of education in the form and manner prescribed by the commissioner. The commissioner may request additional information as necessary.

(b) The report must include:

(1) the number and type of in-person and online teacher professional development opportunities provided by the Minnesota Council on Economic Education or its affiliated state centers;

(2) a description of the content, length, and location of the programs;

(3) the number of preservice and licensed teachers receiving professional development through each of these opportunities;

(4) summaries of evaluations of teacher professional opportunities;

(5) a list of the number, types, and summary evaluations of the direct-to-student ancillary personal finance programs that are supported by grant money; and

(6) a description and the status of all economic and financial literacy education research and results of the research supported by grant money.

(c) The reports required under this subdivision must be prepared and filed according to section 3.195.

Subd. 4.

Grant payment schedule.

The Department of Education must pay one-half of the amount of any grant money awarded to the Minnesota Council on Economic Education by August 15 of each fiscal year for which the money is appropriated and the other half must be paid by February 15 of that same fiscal year. The Minnesota Council on Economic Education must submit its fiscal reporting in the form and manner specified by the commissioner. The commissioner may request additional financial information as necessary.

Sec. 2. APPROPRIATIONS; MINNESOTA COUNCIL ON ECONOMIC EDUCATION.

Subdivision 1.

Department of Education.

The sums indicated in this section are appropriated from the general fund to the Department of Education in the fiscal years designated.

Subd. 2.

Minnesota Council on Economic Education.

For a grant to the Minnesota Council on Economic Education for providing personal finance programs, economic education, and professional development to teachers:
